acceptance_criteria: All 6 real acceptance criteria (split distinct branch_ids, join wait/fire boundary, join excludes cancelled branch, all-cancelled cancels join+instance, order-independence+exactly-once, REQ-049 merge reuse) each have a genuine test, independently confirmed.
The retired transition_test.exs test is confirmed to actually exercise new behavior correctly (not just deleted/weakened).
mix compile --warnings-as-errors and MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine/ re-run directly with actual output quoted.
No existing test coverage elsewhere in the engine test suite was weakened or removed beyond the one intentionally-retired test.

result.summary: Independently re-ran mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean, no output) and MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine/ (1 property, 84 tests, 0 failures -- matches the reported claim). Each of the 6 AC tests in parallel_gateway_test.exs was read against lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's actual dispatch logic and confirmed non-vacuous: AC1 asserts MapSet cardinality of branch_ids (would catch a bug that reused the same branch_id for all children); AC2 asserts the negative case explicitly (2-of-3 arrivals returns pending=[] and cohort still present) as well as the positive fire case; AC3 asserts fire on the 2nd of 2 *active* arrivals with 1 branch pre-cancelled (would catch a naive received_count==expected_count join that never fires here); AC4 asserts :cancel_join distinguishes from :fire via zero received_from_branches, checked against state_3.status==:cancelled and absence of a token reaching 'e'; AC5 asserts both order-independence (state equality across two orderings) and exactly-once firing (fire_count==1 per ordering plus a stale-replay {:error, :unknown_token_id}/{:error, :unknown_branch_id} check) -- a naive re-fire-on-every-arrival bug would fail the exactly-once assertion; AC6 asserts both structurally (grep count of VariableMerge.merge( call sites ==1, no defp merge/overwrite defined) and behaviorally (variable_overwritten event originates from VariableMerge.merge/3, not from the join-fire's own merge_events which is asserted == []). The AC7 retirement in transition_test.exs was confirmed to genuinely change behavior (old assertion {:gateway_not_yet_implemented,...} vs new {:unknown_node_id,...}), matches the shipped :pass_through dispatch path in transition.ex lines 299-308, and the spec states explicitly this would fail against pre-REQ-051 code (REQ-044's unconditional stub return). git diff main...HEAD --stat -- test/ shows only additions to parallel_gateway_test.exs (339 new lines), targeted modification to transition_test.exs (26 lines, the one intentionally-retired stub test), and the new REQ-051.md spec -- no other test file touched, no coverage removed elsewhere. No @tag :skip or TODO found in either test file or the spec (grep, zero matches). All fixtures are self-built per-test (three_branch_graph/0, instance_state/2, do_split/2 construct fresh state every call), async: true, no Ecto.Sandbox/DataCase dependency, no shared mutable state, no hardcoded secrets/connection strings.
